abstract.title: Abstract
content: The goal of this project will be to physically build the circuit that I had simulated for my graduate research. The research in question surrounded an incremental noise-shaping SAR ADC with a low OSR. My intention with this project is to reproduce the spirit of the paper with discrete components, instead of taping out a chip.

The analog frontend will be built of discrete components, and will involve a bootstrapped sample-and-hold circuit, a Silva-Steensgard delta-sigma modulator, and a SAR ADC using a discrete comparator. I plan to use LTSpice to simulate the analog frontend before assembling it on a custom PCB.

The digital backend, with clocking logic, SAR logic, SPI, and control registers, will all be implemented on an FPGA. I am doing initial digital simulations in Xilinx Vivado before choosing an appropritate FPGA.

introduction.title: Python Simulation
content: To determine the realistic specs for this design, I started with Python simulations. I have a Python model in which I can specify DAC mismatch, the number of quantizer bits, and other similar key specs. I then plan to implement the digital backend first, with an ideal SystemVerilog real number model of the analog frontend. The real number model will match the Python simulation.
I plan to verify the digital backend first using UVM, and only once the digital is written to my satisfaction will I begin the analog frontend.
